html:
Hugo Chávez was the president of Venezuela from 1999 until his death in 2013. He led what he called the Bolivarian Revolution, a socialist project funded by oil.

An army officer from the plains, he led a failed coup in February 1992, in the anger after the Caracazo, and became famous in a brief television speech. Elected president in 1998, he brought in a new constitution in 1999, survived a short coup in 2002 and took firm control of the state oil company.

High oil prices paid for clinics, food and housing in the barrios, and poverty fell. He allied with Cuba and led a wave of left-wing governments in Latin America. But he also weakened the courts, the press and private business, and left the country dependent on oil. His chosen successor, Nicolás Maduro, presided over the economic collapse of Venezuela.
